Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Actor presentation

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Downed player characters, called runners, freeze their idle frame, tilt 1.4 radians, dim, hide their gun and reload/muzzle cues, and display a pulsing beacon. Revival and respawn restore the upright pose. Disconnected living runners use the original gray ghost tint. The logical rig and nameplate stay upright so camera tracking and names remain stable; the body sprite carries the tilt and the beacon stays above it.

The existing weapons/UI sheets supply four muzzle cells and the overhead RELOAD! flag. Shot and hurt journal changes drive short visual cues. Confirmation/update does not restart a cue, cancellation only clears its current identity, and old epoch/tick events cannot replace a newer cue. Generation/warp/epoch boundaries reset transient state. The reload flag and downed pose derive from the displayed player state, including local prediction and remote presentation.

Enemies use attack animation rows while stopped near a living target or preparing a boss slam. They face nearby targets and use the original frame counts and 12-FPS death playback. Observed health loss triggers a short hit flash and wobble. Initial observations, rewinds, and epoch/body replacements establish a baseline without those effects.

The typed view adapter creates a new scene when a simulation slot receives a new entity, including when a zombie slot becomes a barrel. Rotation, facing, and transient cues from the prior entity therefore cannot carry over. Status tint follows the original last-visible-status rule and damaging-status flicker.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/actors_run.sh
RSY_HEADED_HOST=1 RSY_AUDIO_DRIVER=Dummy \
  RSY_ACTOR_CAPTURE=/absolute/existing/output/directory \
  nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/actors_run.sh

The gate uses the actual workbench/game and ordinary firing, damage, reset and enemy lifecycles. It checks cue decay, hidden equipment while down, frozen body animation, respawn, attack facing, death, and a fresh binding after slot reuse. Revival and watched-host-crash fixtures also inspect downed/revived/ghost poses.

See evidence. Native captures use Dummy audio, and this slice has a WASM compile check. Combat feedback now supplies bursts, debris and damage numbers. Wall contacts, grenade views and glob discs now have separate implementation/evidence. Remaining ability/UI presentation, broader browser coverage, hardware listening, playtests and full comparison remain work. No gameplay schema or checkpoint fields changed.

Screen effects now cover lens kicks, vignette and transition veil.

Enemy/loot views now use the typed bridge integration. The older linked actor evidence predates this ownership change; current focused receipts are linked from the bridge assessment.
